sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Blaine, MN?
sections.html:
A Blaine owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as it stands. Blaine is a large suburb, 13 miles from Minneapolis and 20 from St. Paul, so a well-kept house usually draws showings quickly. A house that needs work or has a complicated ownership history is where a direct sale tends to fit.

  • List the house and prepare for buyer financing, an appraisal and repair requests.
  • Sell it yourself, which means you handle disclosures, the deed and recording.
  • Sell for cash to an investor and skip showings and repair negotiations.

Whichever route you choose, the same Minnesota paperwork applies, and the county that records your deed is almost always Anoka County.

sections.h2: What is Blaine like, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Blaine is a fast-growing suburb that sits mostly in Anoka County, with a piece in Ramsey County, and its buyers are mainly commuters and families. The city's own history says the population passed 75,000 by 2025, making Blaine the largest city in Anoka County. It grew from 1,694 people in 1950 to 70,222 in the 2020 census.

The land explains the housing. Sandy soil and wetlands discouraged farming, so dairy and sod farms later gave way to subdivisions. Developers in areas such as The Lakes and Club West dredged ponds and used the sand to raise the building sites, and Sunrise Lake in The Lakes is the largest water body in the city at 158 acres. Laddie Lake, at 77 acres, is the only natural lake.

Main routes are Interstate 35W, Highway 65, Highway 10, Highway 610, University Avenue, Lexington Avenue and Hamline Avenue. The National Sports Center opened in 1990 and the TPC Twin Cities golf course in 2000, and the sports center has more than 50 full-size soccer fields plus an eight-sheet ice arena.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Blaine homes?
sections.html:
Three districts serve Blaine, and the one tied to your address is a real selling point. Anoka-Hennepin covers most of the city, including the area from Highway 65 to University Avenue north of 99th Avenue NE. Spring Lake Park Schools covers nearly everything south of 99th Avenue NE, and Centennial Schools covers the area east of Lexington Avenue and south and east of Interstate 35W.

The city has Blaine High School in Anoka-Hennepin, Centennial High School, and Paladin Career and Technical High School, a public charter school. Because boundaries run along streets and not neighborhoods, two houses a block apart can belong to different districts. Put the district name in your listing or your conversation with a buyer, and confirm it with the district before you quote it.

sections.h2: Does Blaine require a rental license if I am selling a rental house?
sections.html:
Yes, Blaine licenses rental property every year, and a buyer who inherits your tenants takes on that duty. The city's application page lists a $190 fee for a single family rental, attached or detached, and $180 per building plus $10 per unit for multi-family. The license expires on December 31, and owners with three consecutive years without violations qualify for a reduced fee.

Single family rentals get an interior inspection every three years and an exterior inspection every year. If you are selling a rental, hand the buyer the license, the last inspection result and the tenant lease documents. An owner-occupied house that you are simply selling does not need any of this.

sections.h2: What happens at recording and closing in Anoka County?
sections.html:
Anoka County records the deed, and its rules decide whether the document is accepted. Its recording requirements page lists what a transfer deed must carry.

  • State deed tax of .0033 times the net consideration when the price is over $3,000, which matches Minnesota Statute 287.21.
  • A $5 agricultural conservation fee.
  • A completed electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value and its number on the deed.
  • A "Send tax statements to" line with the buyer's name and address.
  • Delinquent taxes paid in full before the transfer.
  • A well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or one of the two well statements the county prints on its page.

Anoka County also explains that Minnesota has two land record systems, abstract and torrens, and that most Anoka County property is abstract, so a title search should look for any documents tied to the lot. Your title company usually handles the filing, but you should know what the list asks for.

sections.h2: How are Anoka County taxes and the homestead handled when a house sells?
sections.html:
Residential homestead property in Anoka County is billed in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and the county notes that late payment brings penalties even if you never received a statement. The county's homestead rules add a point sellers miss: the owner must tell the assessor within 30 days if the home sells or stops being a primary residence, and the county can remove the homestead and impose penalties if no one does.

The same county page says a Certificate of Real Estate Value must be filed with the auditor when a property sells, as Minnesota Statute 272.115 requires. A qualifying disabled veteran can receive a market value exclusion of up to $300,000 on homestead property, so buyers who are veterans may ask about it. Ask your title company to prorate the current half-year at closing so you do not overpay or underpay.

sections.h2: What disclosures does a Blaine seller owe?
sections.html:
Before you sign a purchase agreement for a residential property, Minnesota Statute 513.55 requires written disclosure of material facts you know that could adversely and significantly affect a buyer's use and enjoyment. Section 144.496 adds a radon disclosure: whether tests were done, the latest reports, any mitigation system, a radon warning statement and the Minnesota Department of Health booklet.

The city sits on glacial sand, ponds and wetlands, so basement moisture is a fair thing to document. Gather any sump pump records, past repairs and test results before the first showing so the written disclosure is accurate and complete.

faqs.q: Which county records a Blaine deed?
faqs.a: Anoka County for most of the city. Blaine also reaches into Ramsey County, so confirm your parcel's county on your tax statement before sending any documents.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay deed tax when I sell in Blaine?
faqs.a: Minnesota's state deed tax is imposed on the deed and is calculated at .0033 of the net consideration above $3,000. Ask your title company who pays it under your purchase agreement, since the agreement decides that.

faqs.q: Is a rental license transferable to the buyer of my Blaine rental?
faqs.a: Check with Blaine Housing Services before closing. The license is issued yearly and expires on December 31, so the new owner should expect to apply for their own and schedule any inspection the city requires.

faqs.q: What if my Blaine house has radon or basement water problems?
faqs.a: Disclose what you know in writing. Minnesota law requires disclosure of known radon test results and of material facts that could significantly affect a buyer, and a seller who skips them can be held liable for damages.

faqs.q: How long does a Blaine house usually take to sell for cash?
faqs.a: It depends on the buyer and the title work, but a cash sale has no lender appraisal, so closing is often a matter of weeks. Anoka County's recording checklist is the main step that can delay a closing if something is missing.
